articles.title: USA Crude Oil Stocks Rise Week on Week
articles.description: Commercial crude oil stocks, not including the SPR, came in at 418.906 million barrels on November 20, the EIA's latest weekly petroleum status report revealed.

articles.title: Iran, Turkey Extend Natural Gas Deal
articles.description: Turkey extended its long-term natural gas import contract with Iran, according to people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: Eni, Petronas Receive Indonesian Approval for Geliga Gas Project
articles.description: The project targets 5.9 trillion cubic feet of gas in place and 250 million barrels of associated condensate.

articles.title: Forte reports up to 5.8bbbl of prospective oil at Harrier, Alaska
articles.description: Forte Energy has received an independent assessment of up to 5.8bbbl of recoverable prospective resources at its Harrier prospects in Alaska.

articles.title: SAFE Ends Strike at Reach Subsea
articles.description: Members of the Norwegian union of energy workers SAFE voted in favor of a new offer by Reach Subsea, ending nearly a month of strike.

articles.title: Saipem Bags New Middle East Deals Worth $650MM
articles.description: The deals are the latest in a line of Middle East contracts, which are worth billions of dollars, Saipem's website shows.

articles.title: Brent Heads for 1st Weekly Gain in 5 Weeks
articles.description: The Brent oil price is heading for its first weekly gain in five weeks, Saxo Bank highlighted.

articles.title: OPEC+ Faces Growing Pressure As Iraq Pushes for Higher Quota
articles.description: Iraq is negotiating with OPEC for permission to produce more oil, Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said Friday, arguing that the country needs a higher production ceiling to develop its energy infrastructure. The request comes ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meetings on production policy for 2027. For now, Iraq isn't likely to get what it wants. Three sources told Reuters that OPEC+ members have agreed in principle to leave their production quotas unchanged for the first quarter of 2027. That is not yet an official decision, and the group still has…

articles.title: The Oil Glut Everyone Expected Is Looking Increasingly Elusive
articles.description: Brent rebounded to $96 as Houthi attacks and tightening physical supplies raise the prospect of $100 oil despite oversupply forecasts. Friday, November 27, 2026 Oil prices are set to post a slight weekly gain, ending a three-week cold streak, with ICE Brent moving up to $96 per barrel on the back of recurring Houthi strikes on key Saudi energy infrastructure, such as the Jizan and Ras Tanura refineries. articles.title: Soaring Fuel Prices Threaten to Push More Airlines Into Bankruptcy
articles.description: More airlines could soon collapse, the boss of Easyjet has warned, as soaring fuel costs push carriers to the brink. Kenton Jarvis, the company’s chief executive, said Easyjet had sought to swerve the surge in jet fuel prices via a process known as hedging, in which fuel contracts are bought in advance to avoid exposure to short-term price volatility. As much as 69 per cent of the firm’s fuel consumption for the year to September had been hedged at “favourable rates” compared to current prices, Jarvis said. But other…

articles.title: Oil Surge Pushes Indonesia to Mull First Subsidized Fuel Price Hike in Years
articles.description: Indonesia, the largest economy in Southeast Asia, has discussed hiking the price of subsidized fuel for the first time since 2022, as the weakening local currency and persistently high oil prices weigh on government outlays for funding the subsidies. Indonesia, the world’s fourth-most populous country, hasn’t removed or reduced subsidies for gasoline and fuel amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The country, a net oil importer despite having domestic oil production, has subsidized fuel in one form or another since it gained independence…

articles.title: CB&I wins five-year extension from Serica Energy in UK North Sea
articles.description: Chicago Bridge & Iron Company (CB&I) has secured a five-year contract extension from Serica Energy for well delivery and well operatorship services in the UK North Sea.

articles.title: Petronas and Staatsolie approve $1.6bn FID for Suriname gas field
articles.description: Petronas, via its subsidiary Petronas Suriname, and Suriname’s state oil company Staatsolie have announced a $1.6bn final investment decision (FID) for the development of the Sloanea gas field in Block 52 offshore the South American nation.

articles.title: Copper Heads for First Weekly Gain Since Early October After 6.5% Surge
articles.description: Copper on the London Metal Exchange is on track to post the first weekly gain in nearly two months, as prices continued to rally on Friday amid improved risk sentiment. After hitting a record high of over $15,000 per ton on the LME in September, copper prices pulled back sharply over the following weeks, as concerns about global AI investments and the Nvidia spy/love/CEO ousting story dragged AI stocks and equity markets lower. But this week, copper prices are on track for a 2% weekly gain. This would be the first weekly increase for copper prices…

articles.title: Petronas Greenlights Suriname's 1st Offshore Gas Project
articles.description: Petronas and Staatsolie made a positive Final Investment Decision to develop the Sloanea field offshore Suriname for liquefied natural gas production.

articles.title: Trump Urges Putin to End Aggression as Europe Braces for U.S. Military Cuts
articles.description: US President Donald Trump has called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt all military aggression in Europe to pave the way for a Ukraine peace deal, even as Washington postpones a major overhaul of its military footprint on the Continent. In a Truth Social post, Trump wrote that during recent talks in China with Putin, he pressed the Russian leader to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." articles.title: U.S. Encouraged Iraq and Venezuela to Leave OPEC, Sources Say
articles.description: The U.S. Administration early this year encouraged two of OPEC’s five founding members, Iraq and Venezuela, to leave the cartel, Reuters reported on Friday, quoting multiple sources with knowledge of the matter. Iraq and Venezuela have brushed aside this push from the Trump Administration, so far. The U.S. Administration wanted oil production in both Iraq and Venezuela to increase, and was concerned that the OPEC and OPEC+ agreements and production quotas would hamstring any output gains. In Venezuela’s case, the U.S. has had leverage…

articles.title: Deadly Houthi Strike at Jazan Refinery Halts Some Operations
articles.description: An attack on Saudi Arabia's oil refinery in the southern province of Jazan temporarily halted some of the facility's operations and killed one worker, the latest assault by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on the kingdom's energy assets.

articles.title: South Sudan Readies Licensing Round to Boost Oil Production
articles.description: South Sudan plans to launch a licensing round for five blocks as it looks to boost its oil production in the coming years, caretaker Petroleum Minister Awow Daniel Chuang said at an industry event in the country. The upcoming licensing round is part of South Sudan’s push to commercialize the country’s 14 available greenfield blocks and increase crude oil production from just under 170,000 barrels per day (bpd) at present to 200,000 bpd within the next two to three years, the official said at the South Sudan Oil & Power 2026…

articles.title: Australia passes law mandating LNG exporters supply local market
articles.description: The Australian Parliament has passed the Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme (DGRS) obliging liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporters to supply up to 20% of their annual export volumes to the Australian market.

articles.title: Baghdad Moves to Seize Control of Kurdish Oil and Borders
articles.description: Politics, Geopolitics & Conflict Baghdad has ordered a federal takeover of Kurdish oil exports, border crossings and the oilfields under Kurdish security control, and Iraq's Federal Supreme Court has ruled that borders, customs and oversight of oil exports belong to the federal government. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's November 24 order hands every crossing in the Kurdistan Region to the federal Border Ports Authority. articles.title: The Next Hormuz?
articles.description: The approach to the Bab el-Mandeb, the chokepoint at the southern end of the Red Sea, is fast becoming the next Hormuz or Yemen, with Turkey and the UAE building rival military positions along Somalia's coast. In the past week, Somalia ordered the UAE's ambassador out; satellite imagery confirmed that the UAE has built air-defense bases at Berbera in breakaway Somaliland and Bosaso in semi-autonomous Puntland, both on the Gulf of Aden, and Turkey broke ground on a headquarters for Somalia's navy in Mogadishu. The two rivals now hold military positions…

articles.title: Stockpiling Will Support Oil Prices in 2027, Energy Aspects Says
articles.description: Depleted inventories are setting the stage for a major stockpiling push next year, which will support oil prices despite an expected market surplus, Energy Aspect’s founder and director Amrita Sen told Bloomberg TV in an interview on Friday. China will lead the global stockpiling in the coming months, as it typically does when oil prices fall. articles.title: Iraq Boosts Oil Exports to 3.6 Million Barrels per Day
articles.description: Iraq has raised its oil exports to 3.6 million barrels per day (bpd), its oil minister said as OPEC’s second-largest producer seeks a much higher production capacity and quota baselines from the cartel. Iraq’s oil exports increased to 3.6 million bpd, Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) in an interview this week.
